assessment: The `tb cold` tooling is careful at the byte level: tars are written to .tmp, renamed to .unverified, verified with `tar -d`, and confirmed in Mega by size and mtime; every external command (tar, gio, mega-*, docker) goes through execFile/spawn with argument arrays and SQL is parameterised, so there is no injection surface. The weak point is the record's state model. It cannot say what a tar physically contains separately from what the catalog wants it to contain (`held.version` and `next_version` serve both), and the state 'planned' means both 'never made' (droppable) and 'must be sent again' (not droppable). That one gap produces the critical bug (a change noted while a tar is packed/queued is written down as stored, and evict then deletes the only copy of the new files, TCL-01), the audit staging misfire (TCL-04), and the loss of the tar-to-partition map whenever a once-stored tar goes back to 'planned' (TCL-03). Recommended restructuring: (a) record per held row the version/files/bytes a tar was actually packed with and promote only that on confirmation; (b) never let dropPlanned touch a tar that was ever stored, and decide on a distinct 'lost' state for tars Mega no longer holds correctly; (c) have destructive paths re-validate at the moment of removal (evict re-survey, audit re-check) instead of trusting a survey taken minutes or hours earlier. Robustness gaps: a fast-failing Mega makes runs (including --watch) exit silently with code 0 (TCL-02); long-running processes never see new instrument directories (TCL-06); the --cleanup watch guard is bypassed with several trees (TCL-08); an unreadable upload queue disables pacing (TCL-09); pull fails across volumes (TCL-11); abandoned Mega checks keep commands alive (TCL-12). Efficiency: quadratic array spreads over groups of 10^5 items and full-table/ledger re-reads per partition (TCL-16..18). Testing: 260 tests pass but the push state machine (2.4%), evict orchestration (0%), lock and watch loop are essentially untested, and tests are never type-checked; that is where most of these bugs live (TCL-13, TCL-24). Docs: several docblocks argue from the old part/member design, legacy/ is ~2,500 lines of dead, non-compiling code with a README that contradicts COLD-AUDIT.md, and docs/tooling COLD-EVICT.md, COLD-AUDIT.md, COLD.md and docs/planning/COLD.md contain claims these bugs make false. Given the user's fresh-start goal, delete legacy/ and fix the docblocks now (TCL-14, TCL-19), and revise the docs/ pages together with the corresponding code fixes, not before. Reproductions are under reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/.

items.title: A partition that changes while its tar is packed or queued is written down as stored at the new version, though the tar holds the old bytes
items.problem: `noteChange` writes next_version/next_files/next_bytes for a held row in any tar state, but moves only a 'stored' tar to 'stale'. A 'packed' or 'queued' tar (holding V1 bytes, uploading for hours) keeps its state. When the upload is confirmed, step 'queued' calls `record.applyChanges`, which copies every pending next_* into version/files/bytes regardless of what was packed. The record then says Mega holds V2 while Mega holds V1. A corrected tar (packed with V2 in 'fetched') has the same problem if the partition moves to V3 before confirmation. Evict trusts `storedOf` (version == catalog version, next NULL), so it removes V2's files from disk, which exist nowhere else; a later pull returns V1 files labelled V2. The noteChange docblock ('A tar not made yet never gets here') is false.
items.evidence: Reproduced independently three times against the dist build and the real record module: reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/cold/repro1.js, reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/cold/v2/repro.mjs, reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/repro/stale.test.ts, reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/v2/f1.ts. Sequence planTar(V1) -> packed -> move('queued') -> noteChange(V2) prints 'state after noteChange: queued'; applyChanges + stored (exactly step.ts:118-119) yields storedOf ['V2']. tars.ts:112 `if (tar.state === 'stored') move(db, tar.id, 'stale');` is the only state change. plan() runs at every push start and every watch rescan while tars upload; dropPlanned only removes 'planned' tars so packed/queued tars reach noteChange. record.test.ts:83 locks in the behaviour (noteChange then applyChanges with no correction).
items.fix:
Record what each tar was actually packed with and apply only that.
1. schema.ts: add nullable `packed_version TEXT, packed_files INTEGER, packed_bytes INTEGER` to `held`. Because the schema is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, add guarded `ALTER TABLE held ADD COLUMN ...` in `open()` for existing databases.
2. step 'planned': in the same transaction as `record.packed`, set packed_* = version/files/bytes for every held row of the tar.
3. step 'fetched': after `replaceMembers` succeeds, in the same transaction as `record.packed`, set packed_* = the next_* snapshot used to build the correction for changed rows (COALESCE(next_*, version/files/bytes)). Leave version and next untouched so the 'packed' missing-local-file branch (handle -> 'stale') still describes Mega's older tar.
4. Replace `applyChanges` with a confirmation helper used at step.ts:118-119, in one transaction: set version/files/bytes = packed_* where packed_version IS NOT NULL; clear next_* only where next_version = packed_version; clear packed_*; call stored(handle); then if any held row still has next_version NOT NULL, move the tar to 'stale' so the normal fetch-and-correct runs.
5. Rewrite the noteChange docblock: a tar in flight keeps the change noted, to be picked up at confirmation.
Alternative (no schema change, from one verifier): at confirmation, before removing the local tar, read `sizedMembersOf(local)`, and promote next only for rows whose member count/bytes in the tar equal next; otherwise keep next and move to 'stale'. The packed_* route is preferred by both second verifiers as more exact.
items.tests: (a) planTar(V1) -> packed -> noteChange(V2) -> queued -> confirm: storedOf excludes the partition, tar is 'stale', held.version V1, next V2. (b) Same with noteChange while 'queued'. (c) Stored V1, noteChange(V2), fetch+correct (packed_version V2), noteChange(V3) while queued, confirm: version V2, next V3, tar 'stale'. (d) Normal correction with no further change: after confirm version V2, next NULL, state 'stored'. (e) Evict survey holds the partition back in (a) and (c). Rewrite record.test.ts:83 to go through a correction before confirming. Use a step-level test with a fake Remote.
items.verifier_notes: Both lenses found this independently. Lens B's first verifier rated it high (trash default, venue usually still serves the file); both second verifiers and lens A rated critical: silent, permanent corruption of the record that drives a delete. Kept critical. The reviewer's restructuring note applies: the record must separate 'what the tar physically holds' from 'what the catalog wants it to hold'.

items.title: When Mega fails fast, megaCmd waits on an unref'd timer and the process exits with code 0 mid-operation, ending --watch runs
items.problem: A non-timeout failure with mega-whoami also failing (session expired, server down) goes to `untilAnswering`, which waits with `pause` = `setTimeout(...).unref()`. Nothing else holds the event loop (progress interval unref'd, children exited, sqlite sync), so Node drains the loop and exits 0 before megaCmd settles. The 'exit' handler releases the lock; `endured()` never sees an error; --watch stops silently and cron sees success. Contradicts the megaCmd docblock ('rides out an outage of any length') and the reasoning in the `hold` docblock. Separately, push, push vault, pull archives, pull vault and pull needed call `error()` and `return` with exit code 0 when `mega.available()` is false at start.
items.evidence: Reproduced by both lenses and both second verifiers: reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/cold/repro2.js and reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/repro/unref.js print 'Mega is not answering - waiting for it...' then exit 0 with megaCmd never resolving. exec.ts:224 `let pause = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, ms).unref(); });`. `_test_with` assigns one sleeper to both `pause` and `hold`, so tests cannot see the difference. logger.ts:44-46 `error()` only prints.
items.fix:
1. In `untilAnswering` replace `await pause(wait)` with `await hold(wait)` (or `counted(wait)` then `waitingFor(null)` to show the same countdown as the timeout path).
2. Delete `pause` and its comment (exec.ts:223-224); nothing else uses it. Make `_test_with` set only `run` and `hold` (or take separate stand-ins).
3. Rewrite the megaCmd docblock bullet to say the wait holds the process.
4. In the five `mega.available()` false branches set `process.exitCode = 1` before returning (as trusted.ts:14 and evict/archives/index.ts:88 already do).
items.tests: Spawn a child node process (process.execPath) that loads exec with `_test_with(runner, null)` where the runner rejects `{code:1, killed:false}` for the first N calls (including mega-whoami) and then succeeds; assert the child prints 'megaCmd returned' and does not exit 0 before the runner succeeds. Or check `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` contains a Timeout while pending. Add a test that push run with available() false sets exitCode 1. Update mega.test.ts for the new `_test_with` signature.
items.verifier_notes: Unanimous across four verdicts. High: a long-running watch stops doing work without saying so; no data corruption since runs resume.

items.title: Once-stored tars moved back to 'planned' are deleted with their partition map by the next plan(); audit applies this unasked, even on an empty listing
items.problem: `dropPlanned` deletes every 'planned' tar and its `held` rows on every plan(), assuming 'planned' means never made. But confirmTars (size mismatch or not found on the second look), the audit's `again` fix for missing/resized tars (applied to 'stored' and 'stale'), and the byWeight fix move tars Mega holds back to 'planned'. The next push erases the record's only mapping of those partitions to their Mega object. Evicted partitions can then never be pulled (pullableOf needs held rows) or re-packed (they fail 'not on disk as the catalog says' forever), and `MAX(seq)+1` can reuse the remote name. `again` is not marked destructive, so it is the default and runs under --yes. `listing()` turns 'Couldn't find' into an empty map, so a wrong MEGA_ROOT or another logged-in account makes every stored tar 'missing' and `tb cold audit --yes` wipes the whole tar-to-partition map. The vault path is analogous: move to planned + dropVaultPartition, then `round()` finds an evicted file missing locally and calls `dropVaultRevision`, forgetting files only Mega has.
items.evidence: Reproduced with reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/f3/f3.test.ts against real record/confirm/audit modules: confirmTars mismatch leaves state=planned with handle=H1; dropPlanned returns 1; heldOf, tarById and pullableOf all empty. againstMega with an empty listing yields 'not in Mega' with destructive undefined (its own note says cold storage was the only copy); applying it and dropPlanned removes every held row. tars.ts dropPlanned SQL has no handle/stored_at condition. step.ts:94 shows the intended distinction (`tar.handle ? 'stale' : 'planned'`).
items.fix:
Bounded guard now:
(a) dropPlanned: restrict both DELETEs (subquery and tar delete) to `state = 'planned' AND handle IS NULL AND stored_at IS NULL`. A once-stored tar sent back to 'planned' keeps its held rows; its 'planned' step re-packs from disk where every partition matches, otherwise errors each round while keeping the mapping.
(b) Fix the confirm.ts:78 comment so it does not promise a repack that cannot happen once partitions are evicted.
(c) audit/checks/mega.ts: if the listing of megaRoot is empty while the record has tars in 'stored'/'stale' (or vault files 'stored'), return one finding with no solutions saying MEGA_ROOT or the account is likely wrong. Set `destructive: gone(list) > 0` on the tar `again`, and `destructive: list.some(f => f.evictedAt !== null)` on the vault `again`, so neither defaults nor runs under --yes when cold storage is the only copy.
(d) push/vault/work.ts round(): never dropVaultRevision a file that has evicted_at, a handle or stored_at set; report and skip.
Do not route missing/resized tars to 'stale': step 'stale' would queue a download of an absent file and 'fetching' would cycle forever on a size mismatch.
items.tests: confirm.test.ts: stored tar, size mismatch, then dropPlanned -> heldIn(id) and the tar row still exist. planning.test.ts: a once-stored tar moved to planned survives plan(), and plan does not plan a duplicate tar for its partitions. audit.test.ts: empty listing with stored tars -> no applicable solution, nothing changes under --yes; an `again` finding with an evicted partition has destructive=true and choiceOf returns null under --yes. vault.test.ts: a stored-then-evicted file whose Mega copy is missing is not deleted by round().
items.owner_question: Should there be a dedicated terminal 'lost' state for tars (and vault files) that were stored but Mega no longer holds correctly - kept in the record, excluded from storedOf/pullableOf, reported by audit/stats, and never replanned while any partition is evicted? And should planTar keep a per-venue-month high-water mark so a dropped tar's remote name is never reused?
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F4 and lens B F3. Lens A's verifier rated medium/defer, arguing a correct design needs a new state and that its suggested 'stale' routing is wrong (accepted: that routing is excluded above). Lens B's two verifiers rated high/implement with the bounded guard, and reproduced the empty-listing case, which is plausible operator error. Decision: implement the guard (it only stops deletions), defer the state redesign.

items.title: The audit's staging check flags every corrected tar as wrong, and its default fix erases that tar's record
items.problem: For packed and queued tars `differs()` compares members against the held row's current files/bytes. A corrected tar holds next_* until it is stored (applyChanges runs only at confirmation), so any correction that changes count or bytes is reported as 'does not hold what the record says' (even '2 files in the record and 2 in the tar' for a bytes-only change). The fix is not destructive, so it is the default and runs under --yes: it deletes the staged tar and moves it to 'planned', and the next dropPlanned deletes the tar row and all held rows although Mega holds it (it has a handle). The note 'nothing is evicted before its tar is stored' is false for corrected tars. The realistic trigger is an interrupted push leaving a corrected tar packed/queued, exactly what the check targets.
items.evidence: Reproduced by reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/cold/repro3.js and reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/v-F3b/repro.js: FINDING '... is 2 files in the record and 2 in the tar', destructive false; after apply: state planned, handle H:old, tar file gone; dropPlanned leaves 0 held rows, pullable 0; replanned remote is the same name. Existing tests (audit.test.ts:331-380) do not cover a corrected tar.
items.fix:
1. Pass the tar into `differs()` and compare each held row against what the tar was packed with: packed_* when TCL-01's columns are present, otherwise `tar.handle !== null && one.next ? one.next : one`. Report files and bytes in the message.
2. In the fix's apply: rm the staged file, then `record.move(db, id, tar.handle ? 'stale' : 'planned')` (mirroring step.ts:94). Reword the label accordingly.
3. Make the note conditional: claim the partitions are on disk only when no wrong tar has a handle and none of its partitions has an unreturned eviction; otherwise say how many are evicted (as `lost()` in audit/checks/mega.ts does).
TCL-03(a) additionally protects against the dropPlanned erasure.
items.tests: audit.test.ts 'what is left in staging': (a) stored tar with handle, noteChange to different files/bytes, staged tar holding the new members, state packed then queued -> no finding. (b) Same but the staged tar matches neither version -> finding; after apply the state is 'stale', held rows remain with next set, the file is removed, and dropPlanned removes 0 tars. (c) A never-stored wrong tar still goes to 'planned'.
items.verifier_notes: Unanimous (high) across first and second verifiers. Independent of the larger state-model question.

items.title: The audit's 'remove their files again' permanently deletes archive files cold storage may not hold, while docs call it safe
items.problem: For every partition with an unreturned eviction row that has files on disk, the audit offers 'Remove their files from the disk again' via `discard(..., true)`, an `fs.rmSync`, not the trash. It never checks that cold storage holds the partition at the catalog's version. The documented reason an evicted partition has files again is that it changed and only the changed files were downloaded (COLD-EVICT.md); those V2 files exist only on disk and push's correction needs them. Once deleted, correctionOf returns null and push fails forever; the catalog still says downloaded so they are not re-fetched. The docblock ('Neither is a loss - cold storage holds all of it either way') and COLD-AUDIT.md ('Nothing here is a loss') tell the operator it is safe. `evict --cleanup` does make the version check; the audit does not. The vault branch is safe on content (current revision, 'stored', same size) but also purges instead of using the trash.
items.evidence: Reproduced with reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/f8-repro.test.ts: store P@v1, noteEviction v1, noteChange v2, write the changed file, againstDisk returns the finding, applying solutions[1] deletes the file outright. Mitigation: the option is marked destructive so it is never default and never applied under --yes; an operator must pick it, guided by text saying it is safe.
items.fix: In disk.ts `archives()`: split partitions with files on disk. Offer removal only for those that `survey(db, config, origin, venue, stockedIn(config.vaultRoot), Date.now(), looking.archives)` puts in `ready` (i.e. stored at the catalog version, next NULL, stocked) - same rules as `evict --cleanup` - and whose eviction row matches that version. Others get only 'Write them down as back', with a note that the files are newer than cold storage's copy. Change both discard calls (vault :45, archives :68) to purge=false (trash). Rewrite the disk.ts:16-18 docblock; COLD-AUDIT.md:53/60 must be corrected in the same change (docs unit).
items.tests: audit.test.ts 'the archives, against the disk': eviction at v1, held next=v2 (or catalog v2), file on disk -> no removal solution offered. Stored == catalog == evicted version -> removal offered and apply calls discard with purge=false (mock discard or stub gio).
items.verifier_notes: Both verifiers confirmed high. Line numbers in the original finding were stale (disk.ts is 70 lines); corrected above.

items.title: The Archives instrument list is cached for the life of the process: watching pushes never pack tars of new instruments, evict leaves their files
items.problem: `Archives.instrumentsOf` lists each dataset's FL/symbol directories once and caches them forever. Push builds one Archives per work() (outside the for(;;) loop) and evict one per runEvict reused by every pass; both run for days under --watch (single origin). A symbol listed after start is invisible: in push, filesOf undercounts, `matches()` fails in step 'planned' and in corrections, every round until restart (`failed.clear()` does not reset the cache). In evict, monthDirsOf skips the new instrument but noteEviction still records the partition (fewer files), so those files stay on disk unless --cleanup. With several origins each() calls the runners afresh, so the single-origin watch is the affected case.
items.evidence: Reproduced: reviews/2026-11/units/scratch/cold/repro4.js (same Archives 1 file, fresh Archives 2 files) and the second verifier's f4.test.ts (filesOf and monthDirsOf on the same instance miss NEWUSDT/202610).
items.fix: Scope the cache to one look at the catalog. push/archives/work.ts: make `archives` a `let` and reassign `new Archives(config.sourceRoot)` after each watch scan (next to `failed.clear()`), or create it per round alongside `roundOf`. evict: drop `archives` from `Run` and create the Archives at the top of `pass()`, passing it to survey and remove. Optionally add `Archives.forget()`. Update the disk.ts docblock to say the list lasts one pass.
items.tests: disk.test.ts: filesOf on month A, add a new instrument directory with a file for month B; a new Archives (or after forget()) includes it in filesOf(B) and monthDirsOf(B). work() watch test with a fake Mega: a planned tar whose partition includes an instrument created after an earlier round packs on the next round. Evict watch test: a later pass discards the new instrument's files and noteEviction records the full count.
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F6 (verifier: medium, no data lost) and lens B F4 (both verifiers: high, watch push stalls in ordinary conditions since crypto venues list symbols constantly). Took high.

items.title: Evict does not re-check between its survey and the removal, so a partition that changed in between can be removed while cold storage holds only the older version
items.problem: `pass()` surveys every venue, waits on an unbounded prompt (first pass), then removes venue after venue (hours for large venues). `remove()` never re-reads the record or the catalog and discards every file whose name parses to the partition, whole month directories included. If the catalog moves a selected partition to V2 in that window (republish downloaded), the V2 files are removed though cold storage holds only V1, and push's correction then fails every round. COLD-EVICT.md's 'Running it alongside a push ... They do not meet' depends on the survey still being true at removal time.
items.evidence: Code trace (no re-validation between survey, agreed() and remove()). Lens B F9's verifier independently identified the same mid-run residue while refuting B F9's broader claim (disk cannot get ahead of the catalog's version because the hauler only downloads listed files). Removal defaults to the trash, so it is usually recoverable unless --purge.
items.fix: In `pass`, re-survey each venue immediately before removing it and remove only partitions still ready at the same version: `const now = await survey(db, config, origin, one.venue, stockedIn(config.vaultRoot) ?? stocked, Date.now(), archives)`; filter `one.ready` to ids@version present in `now.ready`. In remove(), add a per-partition guard: the partition must still be in `record.storedOf` at partition.version with next NULL (read once per venue as a Set). Do NOT add a disk count-equality check: it would break --cleanup and the documented rule that whatever the archives hold of a passing partition goes. Optional: skip a partition whose on-disk name count exceeds `partition.files` (growth only).
items.tests: Survey, then change the catalog stub's version for one partition (or noteChange it), then run pass/remove: its files remain and no eviction row is written for it. A partition unchanged between survey and removal is still removed.
items.verifier_notes: Lens A rated high; its verifier lowered to medium (narrow window, trash default). Kept medium.

items.title: evict --cleanup gets past its 'not with --watch' guard when several trees are watched
items.problem: With several origins and --watch, `each()` calls `setWatch(false)` and repeats rounds itself, so runEvict's `if (options.cleanup && isWatch())` reads false. `tb cold evict --watch --cleanup` with the default 'all' (or -a) runs cleanup every 30 minutes, undoing pulls - exactly what the guard, the option help and COLD-EVICT.md forbid. Related: in the same loop runEvictVault with an empty selection re-evicts everything (prompt answered by setYes after round one), so vault files pulled for a replay are evicted again within 30 minutes.
items.evidence: Trace confirmed by all three verdicts: cli.ts:43-45 `const watching = several && staying; if (watching) setWatch(false);`. Cleanup only removes partitions stored at the catalog version and uses the trash by default, so it undoes pulls rather than losing data.
items.fix: Check in evict/command.ts before `each()`: read `command.optsWithGlobals<{ watch?: boolean }>().watch`; if it and `options.cleanup` are set, print the existing error, set `process.exitCode = 1` and return. Or add `requestedWatch()` in options.ts that `shared()` sets and `each()` never changes, and have the guard read it. Keep the runEvict guard for direct callers.
items.tests: Register cold + evict on a commander program with runEvict mocked; parse `cold evict --all-sources --watch --cleanup`; assert runEvict is never called and exitCode is 1.
items.owner_question: Should `cold evict --watch` with no selection keep re-evicting the whole vault every round (and therefore files pulled with `cold pull vault`)? COLD-EVICT.md:7 says the vault is evicted 'on request, by a selection' while the evict/vault.ts docblock calls an empty selection ordinary housekeeping; pick one and make both agree.
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F11 and lens B F5. The vault re-eviction half follows from documented semantics plus watch, so it is deferred to the owner.

items.title: An unreadable or unparseable upload-queue summary counts as an empty queue, turning packing pacing off
items.problem: `queue()` returns `{remaining: 0}` both on error and when `parseSummary` returns null, contrary to the file's own 'Unknown is not empty' rule for `queuedPaths`. A drained queue still prints a parseable line, so null genuinely means unknown. `room()` is then always true and push packs a 5 GB tar every round into coldRoot (COLD-PUSH.md measured 133 GB for 2,006 partitions), which can fill the data volume the collectors write to. A mega-cmd update changing the fixed-width summary is the plausible trigger. For the vault, files upload in place, so only the Mega queue grows.
items.evidence: transfers.ts `return parseSummary(stdout) ?? empty;` and `catch { return empty; }`. mega.test.ts 'says nothing rather than guessing when the shape is unfamiliar' shows null is intended as unknown. No free-space check on coldRoot exists in push/.
items.fix: Make `queue()` return `Promise<QueueState | null>` (null on throw or unparseable), warning once with the raw first stdout line. Archives: `room: () => (room ??= mega.queue().then(q => q !== null && q.remaining <= config.queueTargetGb * GB))`. Vault: `room = q === null ? 0 : config.queueTargetGb * GB - q.remaining`. Update `Remote.queue`, stand-ins and any stats/progress callers (show unknown, not 0). Optional: before packing require `statfs(coldRoot)` free >= estimated tar bytes + reserve.
items.tests: queue() with a failing stub megaCmd -> null; roundOf().room() false when queue is null; vault round queues nothing when queue is null; parseSummary unrecognised layout -> null (exists).
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F9 (medium) and lens B F19 (low). Took medium because of the disk-fill path.

items.title: The audit applies fixes long after its checks, without re-validating, while push/evict may be running (can delete a live lock)
items.problem: `runAudit` never acquires a lock; `busy()` is checked only at check time and `settle()` applies each fix after an open-ended prompt. A push started meanwhile can have the audit delete a tar it just queued or move a tar it is correcting. Concretely: the orphan-lock fix lists stale lock files by name and later rm's them; if a new run of that command re-took the lock under the same name meanwhile, the audit deletes a live lock and a second push of that origin can start. An operator running an audit after a crash while cron keeps starting pushes makes this plausible.
items.evidence: No `acquire(` in audit/index.ts; record.ts:22-28 `fs.rmSync(path.join(coldRoot, name))` at apply time. An audit lock alone would not help: acquire only checks its own lock file and push never calls busy().
items.fix: Re-validate at apply time. (1) Orphan-lock fix: recompute `orphans(coldRoot)` inside apply and remove only names still orphaned (holder pid dead). (2) Staging fixes and leftBehind: at the start of apply, if `busy(config.coldRoot)` warn 'another cold command started; skipped' and return. (3) Tar-state fixes (mega.ts:56, tars.ts:64, staging.ts): re-read `record.tarById(db, id)` and move only when state and handle still match what the check saw. Optionally have `settle` re-check `busy()` before any destructive solution, and/or report-but-not-apply when busy at start (not dry run).
items.tests: An orphan-lock finding whose file was rewritten with a live pid (process.ppid) before apply is left in place. A staging finding is not applied when a live lock appears between check and apply. A tar fix is skipped when the tar's state changed after the check.
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F17 (verifier raised to medium for the lock-deletion case) and the audit half of lens B F7. Making audit's purges use the trash is covered by TCL-05.

items.title: pull moves extracted files by rename, which fails with EXDEV when the cold and archives roots are on different volumes
items.problem: `unpack` extracts into `<coldRoot>/pulling/...tar.out`, then `fs.promises.rename`s each member into `config.sourceRoot`. SOURCES_COLD_DIR and DATA_ARCHIVES_DIR are documented as independently movable to other partitions. Across filesystems the first rename throws EXDEV; the error escapes `bring`, the pull (and `pull needed`) aborts, and noteReturn is not called. Usually nothing is moved (partial only when a subtree is its own mount). No data lost (tar stays in pulling, record unchanged), but pull archives cannot work in that configuration. Free space is not checked on sourceRoot. The catalog pull already handles EXDEV.
items.evidence: bring.ts rename with no fallback vs pull/catalog/index.ts:270 `if (code !== 'EXDEV') throw err; copyFileSync; rmSync`.
items.fix: Add a shared `moveFile(from, to)` (shared/fs or shared/disk): try rename; on EXDEV copyFile to `to + '.part'`, rename to `to`, rm source. Use it in bring.ts unpack and replace the private move in pull/catalog/index.ts. Do not stage under sourceRoot (it is walked by Archives and other tools). items.title: backup.check gives up after 20s but the abandoned mega-ls keeps retrying and holds the process open after the command ends
items.problem: `stateOf` races `remote.listing(backupRoot)` and `queuedPaths()` against a 20s timer and never cancels them. mega-ls keeps its 300s timeout; on timeout megaCmd enters the ref'd 'no answer' loop and keeps re-sending. Every command runs `backup.check` via each(), so even `tb cold stats` while Mega is busy stays alive minutes or indefinitely after printing and later prints 'Mega is busy...' lines. Ctrl-C still ends it.
items.evidence: Traced by the verifier: within() has no cancellation; inGroup's detached child and ref'd timer keep the loop alive; the success path never calls process.exit.
items.fix: Add optional `{ timeout?, once? }` to `listing()` and `queuedPaths()` (and Remote + stand-ins), passed to megaCmd. In stateOf call both with `{ timeout: MEGA_MS, once: true }` under one shared deadline; with `once` a timeout kills the process group and throws instead of looping. Keep `within` as a safety net.
items.tests: `_test_with` with a runner that resolves only after its timeout then rejects `{killed:true}`: check() resolves within MEGA_MS and never calls mega-whoami; afterwards getActiveResourcesInfo() has no extra Timeout or ChildProcess.

items.title: Quadratic list building with `[...map.get(k) ?? [], item]` over groups of up to hundreds of thousands of items
items.problem: Each append copies the whole array: O(n^2) per group on the event loop. Partitions span every instrument of a dataset for a month (60k-100k+ files is realistic; the code itself says hundreds of thousands). step 'fetched' does this for every member of a changed partition, and calls idOf three times per member; the audit staging check and vault byVenue do the same.
items.evidence: Verifier benchmark on Node 22: 10k appends 112 ms, 30k 4.4 s, 60k 19.4 s.
items.fix: Add `groupBy<K, V>(items: Iterable<V>, keyOf: (v: V) => K | null): Map<K, V[]>` in shared/ (null skips) using get-or-create then push. Use it at every listed site; compute `idOf(key)` / `remoteOf(file)` / `dataOf` once per item; fix survey.ts:44's `(months.get(...) ?? new Set()).add` similarly.
items.tests: groupBy unit test (order, null skip); one scale test grouping 200k items into one key with a generous timeout (no tight timing assertion).
items.verifier_notes: Lens B only; verifier confirmed with measurements.

items.title: evict vault re-reads and re-parses the whole ledger, and filters all files, for every partition it removes
items.problem: Inside the per-partition loop, `files.filter(...)` is O(F) and `stockedIn(config.vaultRoot)` synchronously reads and parses all of ledger.csv, then `.find`s: O(P*(F+L)) and P full parses. `evictable()` runs twice (each re-reading the ledger and the whole vault_file table), and the ledger is parsed a third time at :69. The per-partition re-read is a deliberate race check (a partition restocked since it was listed must not be removed), so 'once per venue' would weaken it.
items.evidence: vault.ts:155-156 inside `for (const partition of partitions)`; docblock at :36-39 and comment at :158 state the race intent.
items.fix: Group files by partition once (groupBy from TCL-16). Keep the freshness check but cache it: stat the ledger (size, mtimeMs, ino) per partition and rebuild a Map<partition, revision> only when it changed (the ledger is append-only); a missing ledger means an empty map, so every partition is skipped as today. Compute `evictable` once and derive `going`/`kept`; pass the single parsed stockedIn to completable/evictable.
items.tests: Counting spy on the ledger reader: 3 partitions with an unchanged ledger -> 1 parse in remove. Appending a new revision for partition 2 after partition 1 is discarded -> partition 2 skipped and not marked evicted.
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F15 (low) and lens B F11 (medium). Both verifiers reject a per-venue re-read; use the stat-based cache.

items.title: push vault's retire() loads the entire vault_file table for every partition stored
items.problem: `retire` runs per newly stored partition and starts with `record.vaultFiles(db).filter(...)`: a full SELECT with ORDER BY materialised as JS objects to find one partition. A first push of P partitions over F rows materialises P*F objects (~10^9). `unfinishedOf` (ledger parse + GROUP BY) also runs up to three times per loop iteration.
items.evidence: work.ts:247; vaultFiles has no WHERE; the primary key (partition, revision, instrument, side) makes `WHERE partition = ?` an index-prefix range.
items.fix: Add `record.vaultFilesOfPartition(db, partition)` (`WHERE partition = ? ORDER BY revision, instrument, side`); in retire derive `old` and `kept` from that single result. In work(), compute `unfinishedOf` once per iteration and pass it to round().
items.tests: Count vaultFiles calls: storing N partitions in a round makes zero full-table reads. Existing retire behaviour tests (old revision paths not in the new one removed; a failed removal keeps the revision) still pass.
items.verifier_notes: Lens B only; verifier confirmed.

items.title: Taking the lock is check-then-write, and releasing it can delete another run's lock
items.problem: `acquire` checks existsSync and later writes with the default 'w' flag, so two runs starting in the same instant both proceed and fight over dropPlanned/planTar in one record. `give()` removes the file unconditionally, so after an operator overrides a live lock, the first run's exit deletes the second run's lock. The stale check uses only the pid, so after a reboot a reused pid makes an orphaned lock look held and every --yes run fails 'Locked'.
items.evidence: lock.ts:50/82/90. With no await between check and write the race window is microseconds; it needs a cron double-fire or a restart overlap. PID reuse causes refusal, not corruption.
items.fix: Content `pid ${process.pid} since ${iso} token ${randomUUID()}` (optionally boot id from /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id). Create with `fs.writeFileSync(file, content, { flag: 'wx' })`; on EEXIST run the existing stale/held logic, rm, retry 'wx' once; a second EEXIST throws 'Locked - another cold run is in progress'. give(): read the file and remove it only if it still holds this run's token (ignore ENOENT). Treat a lock from another boot id as orphaned in acquire, holders and orphans.
items.tests: Pre-created lock with a stubbed existsSync returning false -> acquire throws instead of overwriting. After a takeover, the first run's give() leaves the second run's file. A lock with a different boot id is cleared without a prompt.
items.verifier_notes: Merged lens A F10 and the lock half of lens B F7. Verifiers rated low (A) and medium (B, including the audit part now in TCL-10); the lock part alone is low. The lock.ts docblock is fixed under TCL-19.

items.title: A pending correction is never cancelled when the catalog version reverts, so the tar is stuck
items.problem: Plan skips a partition when `had.version === one.version || had.next?.version === one.version`. If V1 -> V2 was noted (next=V2, tar stale) and the catalog returns to V1 (identical files re-added; VOCABULARY.md defines a version as the same wherever the same files are), nothing clears next. step 'fetched' calls correctionOf(inTar, disk V1, next V2), which returns null unless counts happen to match, and throws every round; storedOf excludes the partition. If counts match, the correction writes V1 content and the record says V2.
items.evidence: plan.ts:61 has no branch clearing next; step.ts throws '...does not complete what the tar holds of it - left for the next run'.
items.fix: In plan.ts: `if (had.next === null && had.version === one.version) continue; if (had.next?.version === one.version) continue;` and in the remaining case (next set, one.version === had.version) call `record.noteChange(db, had, one)` so next becomes V1 with V1's counts and the correction proceeds toward what disk and catalog hold. Optionally add `record.cancelChange(db, had)` for a tar still 'stale' (not fetched): clear next for that row and, if no row of the tar has next, move it back to 'stored'. Do not cancel fetching/fetched tars.
items.tests: Held row V1, tar 'fetched', next V2, catalog back to V1, disk V1: after plan next is V1; step 'fetched' completes, tar packs, and after landing held.version V1, next NULL.
items.verifier_notes: Lens A only; verifier confirmed low (rare trigger) and refined the fix to reuse noteChange. Coordinate with TCL-01's packed_* columns.

items.title: The catalog push never checks that prospector stayed stopped during the long snapshot copy
items.problem: `stopped()` checks once before copying that prospector and the catalog are down. `writing` is built and stored in Sending but never called. If prospector restarts during a multi-GB copy and a checkpoint lands, the copy is torn but the same size; the only post-copy check is size, and storeSnapshot hashes the copy against itself, so a torn snapshot is stored as the backup. Needs operator error.
items.evidence: grep finds no call of `writing`/`.writing` besides the definition and the state literal.
items.fix: Before the copy record catalogDb mtimeMs and size (and docker `.State.StartedAt`). After `pipeline` in copySnapshot and again after `writePartitions`, fail with the existing 'not a snapshot' message if `await state.writing()` is true, `running(READER)` is true, mtime/size/StartedAt changed, or a `-wal` file now exists. Actually call `writing` (resolves lens B's 'dead writing' point the other way).
items.tests: Stub running so prospector reads true on the second call -> copySnapshot throws and queueCatalogCopy is not recorded. Stub an mtime change -> same.
items.owner_question: Should the catalog snapshot be taken with VACUUM INTO or the SQLite backup API (consistent by construction) instead of a raw byte copy of catalog.db, accepting that the stored file is no longer byte-identical to the live one?
items.verifier_notes: Lens A F14; lens B F18 flagged `writing` as dead and suggested removing it - resolved in favour of using it. Switching to VACUUM INTO/backup API is deferred (changes the documented byte-identical snapshot).

items.title: The vault's --from/--to are not validated; a malformed month silently changes the selection
items.problem: `options.from.replace('-', '')` with no check; months compare as strings. `--to 2025-1` becomes '20251' and selects through 2025-09; `--to 2025` selects through Dec 2024. Only `cold evict vault` is affected (`cold pull` has no --from/--to; it validates --date with monthsOf). Harm is limited (stored current revision only, trash default, totals shown) but the wrong selection is silent.
items.evidence: Verifier checked by hand: '202509' <= '20251' true; '202412' <= '2025' true.
items.fix: Export monthsOf (or move it to shared) and use `from: monthsOf(options.from, '--from').from`, `to: monthsOf(options.to, '--to').to`; a bare year means Jan for --from and Dec for --to; optionally reject from > to. Update the evict help to `<YYYY|YYYYMM>`.

items.title: tar -T lists are read without --verbatim-files-from when packing and correcting, and listings are quoted
items.problem: Without --verbatim-files-from GNU tar unquotes backslash escapes in -T lines (and treats a leading '-' as an option). Listings are quoted by default, so membersOf returns names that differ from on-disk names for unusual characters. Every line starts with `<venue>/`, so the '-' case cannot occur and failures are loud; this is consistency hardening.
items.evidence: Verifier with GNU tar 1.35: a file named `a\nb` fails with plain -T and packs with --verbatim-files-from; listing shows `v/c\\d`.
items.fix: Add --verbatim-files-from before -T at pack.ts:52 and correct.ts:69/74/75, and in the same change add --quoting-style=literal to `tar -tf`/`tar -tvf` in shared/tar.ts (adding verbatim to --delete alone would break the round trip of quoted names). Optionally run listings with LC_ALL=C.UTF-8.
items.tests: tar.test.ts: members `v/c\d` and `v/ü.zip` round-trip through writePart -> membersOf unchanged and through replaceMembers without throwing.
items.verifier_notes: Lens B only; verifier confirmed experimentally and added the listing-side requirement.

items.title: catalog.once() flips a module-global `patient` flag, and catalog fetches have no timeout
items.problem: `once()` sets a global `patient = false` and resets it in finally, so a concurrent ask sees the wrong mode (latent today: both callers are serial). `fetch` has no signal, so a catalog that accepts the connection and never answers holds `once()` (and the push work loop) for undici's 300s header timeout, contradicting 'fails at once'.
items.evidence: catalog.ts:106 fetch without signal; callers traced by the verifier.
items.fix: Add `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(patient ? 120_000 : 15_000)` to fetch (a timeout becomes a connection failure: retried when patient, thrown otherwise). Replace the global with an explicit `{ patient }` option threaded through partitions/readyPartitions/venues, or back once() with AsyncLocalStorage.
items.tests: Stub server that never answers: once(() => venues(config)) rejects within the short timeout. Two concurrent asks, one inside once, against a 503 server: the outer one keeps waiting and succeeds after recovery.
items.verifier_notes: Lens B only.

items.title: Non-null assertions on optional Remote.queueUploads, and modulo-based re-ask timing in storeSnapshot
items.problem: `remote.queueUploads!` asserts away an optional member (only a future stand-in would crash). `waited % ASK_MS === 0` with `waited += pollMs` only works because POLL_MS divides ASK_MS and SAY_MS.
items.evidence: grep of the cited lines; Remote declares `queueUploads?`.
items.fix: Make queueUploads required in Remote (the type checker then enforces stand-ins), or fall back to looping queueUpload. Track lastAsk/lastSay and fire when `waited - lastAsk >= ASK_MS` (same for SAY_MS). The `Sending.writing` part of the original finding is handled by TCL-22 (use it, do not delete it).
items.tests: storeSnapshot with pollMs=7 and small ASK/SAY overrides re-asks after the threshold.
items.verifier_notes: Lens B F18 minus the `writing` removal.

items.title: Helpers and constants duplicated across commands, including two RESERVE_GB with different meanings and a circular import
items.problem: byVenue/bytesOf/loadOf duplicated between evict/vault and pull/vault; freeBytes x3; count x3; RESERVE_GB is 25 in bring.ts and 5 in pull/vault; execFileAsync built in four places; bring.ts imports from its parent index (circular, works only because uses are inside functions); pull/needed reaches into ../archives; evict pass() re-implements trusted() with a watch variant.
items.evidence: grep of the definitions at the cited lines.
items.fix: shared modules for count, freeBytes, and StoredFile byVenue/bytesOf/loadOf; one execFileAsync; rename to ARCHIVES_RESERVE_GB = 25 and VAULT_RESERVE_GB = 5 in config.ts; move asideRoot out of pull/archives/index.ts so bring.ts does not import its parent. Change trusted to `trusted(config, { watching })` returning `{ ok: true, stocked } | { ok: false, retry: boolean }` (pass() needs the stocked value) and use it in pass(). No behaviour change; asserted messages keep their wording.
items.tests: Existing tests pass unchanged.
items.verifier_notes: Lens B only; pure refactor, safe.

items.title: Every command makes a full VACUUM INTO copy of the record and reads it whole into memory to hash it
items.problem: each() runs backup.check/save around every tree (stats and dry runs too, documented as deliberate). stateOf always VACUUMs a full copy and `fs.readFileSync`s it to hash: a synchronous allocation the size of the record, which throws ERR_FS_FILE_TOO_LARGE above 2 GiB so no backup would ever be sent at that size.
items.evidence: backup.ts:200 `createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(copy))`. The watching push saves only on entering a wait (overstated in the finding). PRAGMA data_version cannot detect cross-process changes on a fresh connection, so that suggestion is wrong.
items.fix: Move the streaming `digestOf` from push/catalog/index.ts to shared/ and use it in stateOf. Leave the run-around-every-command policy as is.
items.tests: stateOf/save give the same digest as before; with fs.readFileSync stubbed to throw on the copy path, it still works.
items.owner_question: Should read-only commands and dry runs skip the backup check/save, and should the VACUUM be skipped when the db and -wal size/mtime match what sent.json recorded at the last send?
items.verifier_notes: Lens B F13; only the streaming hash is implemented.

rejected.title: Evict trusts a tar as stored before push's second look (confirmed_at gate) [lens A F7]
rejected.reason: Verifier uncertain, no second verifier: the trigger (Mega losing or replacing a complete file after a size+mtime 'landed' check) is speculative, and a confirmed_at gate changes evict's semantics. Does not survive the vote. Its cheap vault-side safety check (never dropVaultRevision a file that was evicted or stored) is folded into TCL-03(d).

rejected.title: Evict removes whole directories without checking disk matches the catalog version [lens B F9]
rejected.reason: Refuted: the catalog's version comes from the venue listing and the hauler only renames downloads that match it, so disk content cannot get ahead of the catalog. The no-disk-check rule is documented and --cleanup depends on it; an equality guard would break it. The real mid-run residue (catalog moves between survey and removal) is handled by TCL-07.
